about.athena: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.
about.study: A study is Athena's written reading of another software project, taken at one fixed commit so that it describes exactly one version. Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files.

what.text: Firstmate is a tool for people who direct AI coding agents. It keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a worker, a separate AI coding tool that does that one task, so that several tasks can run side by side without the workers overwriting each other's files and without a person starting each agent by hand.
Firstmate takes an item from a backlog and gives it to a worker, which does the work in its own isolated worktree, a separate working copy of the project.

Firstmate's own deciding AI, called the agent on this page and never a worker, decides what to dispatch and how to recover a stuck worker, while scripts enforce the gates: what may be dispatched, when a report is accepted, and when a worktree may be returned.

After a PR or ready branch exists, the task waits for the configured merge authority. With the yolo setting off, the captain approves every PR merge and every local-only landing. With yolo on, firstmate merges green work that is in scope itself, and never a red one.

Tasks are handled differently by kind. A ship changes a project; a local-only ship has no PR and lands by a guarded fast-forward. A scout produces a report and never a PR. A relaunch replaces a stuck worker with a new one. A secondmate is a persistent home, not a backlog item.

limits.text: If another spawn holds the shared project lock, a spawn exits 1 and does not wait.
If the project's capacity declaration cannot be read, a spawn exits 1 instead of guessing the limit. A capacity that is full is a different case: it exits 75 and the item stays queued.
If a relaunch fails after the old agent was stopped, the prior durable record is restored and the report says no agent is running.
The study found no bound on how many times one task is relaunched, and none on how many times a deferred item is dispatched again.

The cited text states no count or limit on retries of a failed backlog close. The next session start retries it, and the cited text names no other retry, so a close is not replayed until a session starts.
The cited text sets no deadline or default for a captain who does not answer.
Finishing work does not free a place. Only a recorded PR or a cleanup does, so a local-only ship or a scout that records no PR keeps its place until cleanup.
A teardown whose backlog item is still an open captain call reopens the item instead of closing it, and --force does not change that. Only the captain's answer closes it.
Yolo never lets firstmate merge a red PR or one with a required check that has not reported, unless a current explicit captain instruction waives the check.

walkthrough.text: The item waits in the backlog as Queued. A spawn is accepted only for an unheld, unblocked item.
Spawning moves the item to In flight and creates an isolated worktree for the worker. If every place of a declared capacity is held, the spawn exits 75 and the item stays queued.
When the worker reports a PR or ready branch, the report is refused while the work exists only in the worker's disposable copy.
A PR-based ship's place is freed once its ready PR is recorded; a local-only ship or a scout keeps its place until cleanup.
The task then waits for the configured merge authority. With yolo off, the captain approves; with yolo on, firstmate merges green work itself.

Teardown returns the worktree only if it is clean and the committed work has landed, and it removes the task record and closes the backlog item as one step. A scout skips the landed-work check because its report is its product.
If the backlog item is still an open captain call, teardown reopens it instead of closing it.
If the backlog close fails, the pending-close record is kept and the next session start retries it.

start_terms.text: The person who directs firstmate and decides whether finished work is merged. See the Glossary entry for captain.
A setting that decides who approves merges: off, the captain approves; on, firstmate merges green work that is in scope itself.
The words firstmate's instructions use for the work that yolo lets firstmate merge itself. The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it.
A PR that is not red: it can be merged under the yolo rule if the work is in scope (defined above).
A PR that is failing, or has a required check that has not reported. It is not merged under either yolo setting unless a current explicit captain instruction names the check to waive.
The last step of a local-only ship, which has no PR: firstmate lands the ready branch by a guarded fast-forward into the main local checkout, once the merge authority approves.
A firstmate home is the place that holds a backlog of tasks. A secondmate is a persistent home of its own, not a task in someone else's backlog.

terms.text: These words appear in the sentences that follow. Each is defined here, and again in the Glossary at the end of the page.

states.text: A state is a stage a piece of work can be in. The list shows all six, from Queued, where an item waits in the backlog, to Done, where its worktree is returned and its backlog item closed, and Reopened, where teardown left the item open for the captain. Done and Reopened both carry the tag "ends the task": the model shows no move out of either. Reopened is not a failure; the item stays open until the captain answers. Read each line as the state's name, its kind, and the claims that support it.

counters.text: A counter is a number that firstmate reads or changes as work moves. The study found one, places-held, which counts the worker places in use against a project's declared capacity. A spawn takes a place; a place is freed only when a worker records its ready PR or is cleaned up. A secondmate holds no place. Read each line as the counter's name and the transitions that change it.

transitions.text: A transition is one move of a piece of work from one state to another. Each card opens with a one-line summary, then gives the trigger that starts the move and the guard that must hold, and says who decides each: the agent or code. The two deciders are explained below the cards' heading. "Decided by agent" always means firstmate's own deciding agent, never a worker.

why.text: Each card here is a design choice the study found, with the alternatives the authors named and what the choice costs. Read a card as: what was chosen, what else could have been chosen, and the trade-off that came with the choice.

deciders.text: Firstmate's own deciding AI. "Decided by agent" on a card means this agent, never a worker, which is the separate AI tool that does one task. The agent judges, for example whether an item is ready to dispatch or a worker needs recovery. Scripts check the shape of its choices but do not make them.
Code is the firstmate scripts. They apply the rule themselves and refuse when it is not met, for example the capacity check and the check that work is reachable outside the worker's disposable copy.

summaries.text: The agent dispatches a queued item: it becomes In flight and its worker gets an isolated worktree.

Every worker place is held, so the spawn is deferred with exit 75 and the item stays queued. A spawn that cannot take the project lock, or cannot read the capacity declaration, exits 1 instead and does not wait. No bound on how often an item is deferred was found.

The worker reports a PR or ready branch and the work becomes Ready, unless the work exists only in the worker's disposable copy. A recorded PR frees the worker's place; a local-only ship has no PR, so its place stays held.

The merge has landed, so teardown returns a clean worktree, closes the backlog item and the work is Done. The captain approved the merge, or yolo was on and firstmate merged it; a local-only ship also counts as landed once it is merged into the local default branch. Cleanup frees the place.

Teardown could not close the backlog item, so the work waits as Close pending and its pending-close record is kept. The cited text names the next session start as the retry and no other; until a session starts, the close is not replayed.
The next session start replays the pending close and the work becomes Done.
A replay of the pending close ended incomplete, so the work stays Close pending. The cited text states no limit on these retries.

A stale wake shows the worker is stuck, so the agent may relaunch it in the same worktree and the work stays In flight. If the relaunch fails after the old agent was stopped, the prior durable record is restored. No bound on relaunches was found. A ship or scout keeps its recorded harness and needs a note; a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none, and a secondmate with no endpoint is recovered by the spawn script instead. A relaunch is not deferred for capacity.

Teardown finds the backlog item is still an open captain call, so it reopens the item with the deliverable recorded instead of closing it. If it cannot tell, it refuses, and --force does not change that.

With yolo on, firstmate merges green work that is in scope (the instructions do not say what qualifies) itself through the merge script, which refuses unless its live conditions hold. The task stays Ready because merging does not end it: it is Done only when teardown later returns the worktree and closes the backlog item (the t4 card), which is also how a merge the captain approved reaches Done. With yolo off firstmate does not merge: the captain approves. A red PR is never merged either way.
A scout's report exists, so teardown proceeds without the landed-work check and the work is Done. A scout never makes a PR and keeps its place until this cleanup.

glossary.definition: The firstmate scripts, as opposed to the agent. They enforce a rule and refuse when it is not met.
The state of an item waiting in the backlog before it is dispatched.
The state of an item whose worker is doing the task in its worktree.
The state after a PR or ready branch exists, while the task waits for the merge authority.
The state of a task whose teardown could not close the backlog item, so a pending-close record waits to be replayed.
The final state: the task record is removed and the backlog close has landed.
The counter of worker places in use. A place is freed only when a worker records its ready PR or is cleaned up. When the counter reaches a declared capacity, a spawn is deferred.
The exit status a spawn returns when it is deferred because every place is held. The item stays queued.
A pull request: the proposed change a worker reports as finished, which the merge authority approves.
The bootstrap step when the agent begins a session; it replays any pending-close record left behind.
A stage a piece of work can be in. The states are listed first, under States of a piece of work.
A move from one state to another, shown as a card with its trigger and guard.
What starts a transition, and whether the agent or code decides that it has happened.
The condition that must hold for a transition to go ahead, and whether the agent or code checks it.
A number that some transitions change and others read, listed under Counters.
One sentence about firstmate, with its sources. Each claim has an id such as c1; the bracketed ids on this page link to the claims listed at the end.
The single firstmate commit the study read, shown at the top and in the footer. Nothing here describes any other version.
The label on a claim that says how the study came to it, shown beside the claim at the end.
A unit of work in a home's backlog. Dispatch refuses an item the home does not have.

Firstmate's own deciding AI, which judges what to do, such as which harness to use or whether to recover a worker. "Decided by agent" on a card means this agent, never a worker. Scripts check the shape of its choices.
The words firstmate's instructions use for the work that yolo lets firstmate merge itself. The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it.
A separate AI coding tool that carries out one task in its own worktree. It is not the agent, which is firstmate's own deciding AI.
A separate working copy of the project, isolated from the primary checkout, in which a worker does its task.
The kind of worker chosen for a dispatch. The agent picks it; scripts validate it.
The script that dispatches a task: it moves the item to In flight and refuses when it cannot.
An optional limit on the places a project has for workers. When all places are held, a spawn is deferred.
The exit status a spawn returns when it cannot take the shared project lock (it does not wait) or when the project's capacity declaration cannot be read.

A kind of task, named next to scouts. Its done report is refused while the work exists only in the worker's disposable copy, and its worktree is returned only when it is clean and the committed work has landed.
The person who approves every PR merge and every local-only landing when yolo is off.

A setting that decides who approves merges. When it is off, the captain approves every PR merge and every local-only landing. When it is on, firstmate merges green work that is in scope itself; it never merges a red PR.
The script that ends a task: it refuses a dirty worktree and removes the task record together with the backlog close, or with a reopen when the item is still an open captain call.
What teardown does to a backlog item that is still an open captain call: it records the deliverable and leaves the item open instead of closing it.
The final state of a task whose backlog item was reopened for the captain instead of closed.
A kind of task that produces a report at data/<id>/report.md and never a PR. Its worktree is scratch and teardown does not check for landed work.
A delivery mode with no PR: the worker stops with a clean ready branch and firstmate lands it by a guarded fast-forward once the merge authority approves.
A persistent firstmate home, not a worker and not a backlog item. It holds no place, relaunches by its own rules and is retired explicitly.
One of a project's worker slots. A recorded PR or a cleanup frees a place; a local-only ship or a scout keeps its place until cleanup, and a worker steered back after its PR is not counted again.
A record kept when a backlog close fails, so a later session start can replay the close.
A PR that is not red: with yolo on and the work in scope (see the entry for in scope), firstmate merges it itself.
A PR that is failing, or has a required check that has not reported. It is not merged under either yolo setting unless a current explicit captain instruction names the check to waive.
The place where firstmate keeps a backlog and the records of its tasks. Spawning refuses work the home has no item for. A secondmate is a persistent home of its own, not an item in a backlog.
A wake after which the agent inspects a worker that may have stopped, looped or gone quiet.
Replacing a running worker with a new one in the same worktree. A ship or scout keeps its recorded harness and needs a note; a secondmate does not.
